evidence.estrutura: Norwegian social-democratic governance and international institutional work support coordinated national policy within democratic decentralization; no structural extreme.
evidence.representacao: Repeated electoral leadership in Norway strongly supports representative democracy and accountable institutions.
evidence.poder: Her public-health governance accepts regulatory authority while remaining within rights-based democratic institutions; moderate state-power placement.
evidence.imigracao: Nordic social-democratic and internationalist politics support relatively pluralist inclusion, though immigration was not her defining field.
evidence.diplomacia: Leadership of WHO and the World Commission on Environment and Development strongly support multilateral diplomacy.
evidence.intervencao: Her international work emphasizes cooperation, development and institutions rather than unilateral force; relatively restrained intervention posture.
evidence.economia: Social-democratic governance supports a mixed economy with strong welfare provision and public coordination.
evidence.controle: Public health, environmental regulation and welfare policy imply substantial regulatory planning without command economics.
evidence.comercio: Her sustainable-development internationalism accepts global economic integration subject to social/environmental rules; relatively open trade.
evidence.religiao: Public policy is secular and technocratic rather than religiously grounded.
evidence.moral: Gender equality, social welfare and human-rights-oriented Nordic politics support moderately progressive values.
evidence.tecnologia: Science-based public health and sustainable-development policy support a strongly pragmatic pro-technology stance constrained by environmental and health goals.
